answers.text: The reply puts the fixes in priority order and says what needs a person
answers.evidence: Both graders: the reply sorts problems into 'Fix before launch' (1-5), 'Accessibility problems to fix next' (6-9) and 'Smaller issues', and its 'Suggested order' says 'Items 1–5 first ... Then 6–9'. It names what it could not check: 'Everything below comes from the code, not from tapping through on a real phone. Please have someone do a quick check on an actual phone before launch, especially items 1 and 4', and asks for the fixed date to be confirmed with the agency.

mapping.title: 'Few left' tag has low contrast (3.0:1 light, 3.4:1 dark)
mapping.reason: First raised in the intro ('dark mode passes contrast everywhere except one tag (item 9)') and stated in full as item 9: '3.0:1 in light and 3.4:1 in dark, for 16 px text. It needs 4.5:1'. This is the D03 contrast failure.

mapping.title: Double tap on 'Book this slot' cancels the booking while the done page still says 'Booked'
mapping.reason: Book 'waits 1.5 s and shows nothing visible', a second tap makes the booking 'saved with status "cancelled"', and the done page keeps the heading 'Booked' and a reference. This is exactly D09.

mapping.title: Five-minute hold never mentioned and runs out without warning
mapping.reason: 'The 5-minute hold is never mentioned, and it runs out without warning'; the resident only finds out after Book, from 'This slot is no longer available' with 'the slot blanked out'. This is the unseen hold running out in D08.

mapping.title: Today opens by default and offers past or too-soon slots that are refused at the last step
mapping.reason: 'Same-day slots less than about 30 minutes ahead get rejected, and only at the very last step after all the details have been typed.' This is D06's offered-then-refused slots.

mapping.title: Today's date and the quick-day dates hard-coded in the bundle
mapping.reason: The reviewer says itself 'I'm assuming this is fixture data, but it needs confirming', and the packet's scenario fixes today as Monday 12 October. It is a deployment check for the agency, not a problem the review shows residents meeting in the flow.

mapping.title: 'Change slot' / 'Back to the slots' reset to Today and silently move the booking
mapping.reason: 'The slots page never reloads the day the resident already chose. It always resets to Today with nothing selected.' This is 'Change slot' forgetting the chosen day, D12.

mapping.title: Van/trailer permit field appears late and unannounced; permit only checked on the confirm page
mapping.reason: The permit field 'only appears 1.2 s later, without any announcement', is not checked on the vehicle page, and is 'only checked after tapping Book on the confirm page, where there's no permit field'. The mapping instructions assign the delayed field and the confirm-page permit error to D07.

mapping.title: No focus outline on slot buttons
mapping.reason: 'The script inserts `.slot:focus{outline:0}` ... so keyboard users can't see which slot they're on.' This is D05.

mapping.title: 'Few left' slots moved out of time order to the top of the grid
mapping.reason: 'Each one gets `order:-1`, so they all move to the top of the grid, above the "Morning" heading', while 'Screen-reader and keyboard order still follow the clock'. This is D10.

mapping.title: Page scrolls sideways on 360 px phones
mapping.reason: 'At 360 px and below, the script gives the slot grid fixed pixel columns that ignore the page padding, so the grid comes out about 30 px wider than the screen.' This is D04.

mapping.title: Slot grid empty for 0.9 s on a day change with no 'Loading slots…' message
mapping.reason: 'Changing the day empties the slot grid for 0.9 s with no "Loading slots…" message': the grid is empty and nothing says slots are coming. That is the wait in D01 (a narrower statement of it).

mapping.title: Status line only becomes a live region after the first load, so the first count is not announced
mapping.reason: 'The status line only becomes a live region after the first load ... Screen-reader users hear nothing the first time.' This is D11.

mapping.title: Vehicle-page error summary links point at non-focusable divs (#vehicle, #waste)
mapping.reason: The links 'go to `#vehicle` and `#waste`, which are divs that can't take focus', so a keyboard or screen-reader resident who follows an error link is not taken to the control to fix. No seeded defect covers this.

mapping.title: Late errors on the confirm page (past slot, permit, centre closed) have no links to where they can be fixed
mapping.reason: 'On the confirm page, the late errors (past slot, permit, centre closed) have no links to where they can be fixed.' A resident stuck at the last step with an error and no route to the fix is genuinely hurt, and the 'centre closed' case is not seeded. Adding links would not stop past slots being offered (D06) or fix the hidden permit rule and delayed field (D07), which the review reports separately as R4 and R7.

mapping.title: Booking reference only on the done screen and in tab storage, not sent by text
mapping.reason: 'The reference only exists on the done screen and in that browser tab's storage, and the centre has poor signal.' Residents must show it at the gate, so losing the tab loses the booking proof. D14 is about the missing day, slot and vehicle, not keeping the reference.

mapping.title: 'Reminder the evening before' promise does not fit late bookings
mapping.reason: Someone booking 'at 9 pm for tomorrow morning' has just seen the booking; the review shows no harm from the missing reminder beyond the wording.

mapping.title: Slot end time and 'Arrive within your slot' only in a tooltip
mapping.reason: 'The slot end time and "Arrive within your slot" are only in a `title` tooltip, which never shows on phones.' This is D13.

mapping.title: Step list numbers read twice by screen readers
mapping.reason: 'The step list is an `<ol>` and also has typed "1." "2." "3.", so screen readers read the numbers twice.' A small but genuine accessibility defect for blind residents, not seeded.

mapping.title: Waste hint not announced by screen readers
mapping.reason: 'The waste hint is attached to a plain div, so screen readers don't announce it', so screen-reader residents miss the guidance on what waste they can bring. Genuine and not seeded.

mapping.title: Registration field does not autocapitalise
mapping.reason: 'The registration field should use `autocapitalize="characters"`' is an input-convenience suggestion; the review shows no harm such as lowercase registrations being rejected.

mapping.title: Theme colours set only by the script after load
mapping.reason: 'If the script fails, the page has no theme at all' is speculative and depends on a script failure that would break the slot booking anyway; the review shows no harm in the working flow.

settled.reason: Alignment and numbering. A R10 and B R1 are the same 'Few left' contrast problem, both mapped to D03. The review first raises it in the intro, 'dark mode passes contrast everywhere except one tag (item 9)', before item 1; the mapping instructions number problems in the order they first appear, a later restatement being the same item, so it is R1 as B numbered it, and A's R1-R9 each move down one. The agreement file's R1 split (A's double tap vs B's contrast) is an artefact of this shift.

Alignment. Both describe item 1, 'Tapping "Book this slot" twice cancels the booking, but the page still says "Booked"', and both map it to D09. The agreement file's R2 split compares A's hold item with B's double-tap item.
Alignment. Both describe item 2, 'The 5-minute hold is never mentioned, and it runs out without warning', and both map it to D08.
Alignment. Both describe item 3, '"Today" opens by default and lists slots that have already passed', and both map it to D06.

Alignment. Both describe the 'Check with the agency' note that 'the bundle has today fixed as `2026-10-12`', and both map it to not-a-problem. The split the agreement file shows at R4 (A not-a-problem vs B D06) compares A's dates item with B's Today item; once aligned the graders agree, so nothing needed settling and the agreed mapping is kept.
Alignment. Both describe item 4, '"Change slot" and "Back to the slots" silently move the booking to today', and both map it to D12.
Alignment. Both describe item 5, 'Van and trailer permits: the field appears late and errors come too late', and both map it to D07.
Alignment. Both describe item 6, 'No focus outline on slot buttons', and both map it to D05.
Alignment. Both describe item 7, '"Few left" slots jump out of time order', and both map it to D10.
Alignment. Both describe item 8, 'The page scrolls sideways on 360 px phones', and both map it to D04.

Mapping decision; the two R14s are the same item ('On the confirm page, the late errors (past slot, permit, centre closed) have no links to where they can be fixed'). A broader or narrower statement maps to a defect only 'if fixing what the review describes would fix the defect'. Adding links to these errors would not stop today's started slots being offered and refused three steps later (D06) or fix the hidden permit rule, delayed field and Next accepting an empty permit (D07); A's own reason concedes it covers only 'the no-way-back facet'. Those defects are already found through the review's own items R4 and R7. The harm this item names, errors at the last step with no route to the fix, including the unseeded 'centre closed' error, is genuine for residents, so B's real-unseeded is what the mapping instructions support.
